findings: formation.type: “derived” is not supported for 体. The entry describes 体 as both a traditional variant and the standardized simplified counterpart of 體, which are complete-character relationships; no distinct inherited formation for the body spelling is established. Set the type to “disputed” or another type that does not assert derivation, and retain the qualified 體 analysis under the historical host. Evidence: X-b5525f891acf53981c53, X-feea8a0c30cfa48ecc41, X-610a1ebe5449fd673c96.

formation.text: “an older variant spelling” asserts that 体 is older than 體, but the evidence only documents 体 as a traditional vulgar variant and records examples from Song–Yuan onward. Remove “older” or qualify the chronology. Evidence: X-b5525f891acf53981c53, X-610a1ebe5449fd673c96.

learner.overview: “simplified form” is accurate, but the second sentence foregrounds the separate, rare bèn reading and spends the short first-reading layer on a peripheral ambiguity. Replace it with a concise explanation of the body spelling; keep the separately recorded bèn sense and its unresolved connection in the expert account. Evidence: X-b5525f891acf53981c53, X-610a1ebe5449fd673c96.
